Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

Cross-cutting acceptance review: verify workflow-owned RSS and headless documentation against the versioned implemented contracts and common published-content visibility foundation. Check discoverability, stable IDs/canonical URLs, updates/withdrawals/freshness, Markus body fields, lists/filter/pagination/assets, errors, public field allowlists and no-draft examples. Verify sample links/requests and permission boundaries using appropriate later tests. Preserve explicit deferred/YAGNI scope and avoid claiming M8 latest/search JSON already provides the new full contracts. Record evidence and remaining gaps.

Cross-cutting post-save review additionally traces PPY-defff04e-17b5-4e28-9bb5-df412601a102 from public-save/publish/unpublish to article, affected listings/indexes, sitemap, both RSS/Atom and enabled headless outputs. Verify shared selection/metadata, no private draft leakage, documented freshness and visible/retryable ancillary failures. Check documentation against actual implemented behavior; no new-service or atomicity assumption.

Approved dependency-guide correction: explain automatic extraction from supported declarative listing/embedded-content constructs at save/compile time and the generated reverse index. Rendering selection is the only source of type/featured parameters; no duplicated manual per-page rules. Cover union across components, old-or-new published-state matching for additions/removals/type/featured changes, and replacement/removal of stale page registrations. Publication visibility is enforced separately. Record unsupported custom-query fallback, exact extension ownership and schema syntax as open design questions. Anth.us main currently generates custom Python listing fragments and hashes them for incremental invalidation; do not present the proposed generic construct or reverse index as already implemented. See foundation PPY-3f55c3 and story PPY-defff0 for pinned source evidence.

Final agreed authoring direction, planning only: “include” is the working construct name, not approved concrete syntax. It supports inclusion of a single page or a selected list. “Collection” means a selection of content, not a new storage object. On page/content save or compile, the supported pipeline scans/parses include constructs, updates the generated site-wide dependency index, and actually uses that index to regenerate affected pages; merely recording dependencies is incomplete. Reuse each include's rendering selection as the sole source of invalidation selection, with separate enforced publication/access/published gates. Nested/transitive includes, cycles, deduplication, edits/deletion and retries require observable behavior, not arbitrary-code inference.

RSS/Atom feed eligibility is distinct from page existence, include membership and navigation. An ordinary static wiki/help or product page does not automatically become a feed entry. Define shared feed selection/metadata and editorial eligibility without building a separate page or wiki engine. Exact include syntax, extension ownership and selection schema remain design questions; current Anth.us custom Python homepage code is evidence of a migration gap, not proof the proposed include construct is shipped.

Detailed include BDD: PPY-b6ede164-fad8-45da-a242-51362c5f8285. Author/operator documentation behavior: PPY-01b5e07f-773e-407f-9057-941f4e4c5a0c. Review must trace these scenarios through actual public output changes and failure recovery when implemented; documentation presence or an index write alone is insufficient.
